input.command:
# Resize/scale to 720 wide so we get better view but smaller files
mkdir -p /tmp/slices
for f in home about action science stories; do
  rm -f /tmp/slices/${f}_*.png
done
# slice into multiple chunks per file
declare -A heights=( ["home"]=4798 ["about"]=5644 ["action"]=7231 ["science"]=7638 ["stories"]=5310 )
for f in home about action science stories; do
  h=${heights[$f]}
  chunk=1900
  y=0
  i=1
  while [ $y -lt $h ]; do
    remain=$((h - y))
    crop_h=$chunk
    if [ $remain -lt $chunk ]; then
      crop_h=$remain
    fi
    ffmpeg -y -i /task/screenshots/${f}.png -vf "crop=1440:${crop_h}:0:${y},scale=900:-1" /tmp/slices/${f}_p${i}.png 2>/dev/null
    y=$((y + chunk))
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
done
ls /tmp/slices/

About the Collective

Founded in 2011. Independent. Science-led.

A 501(c)(3) coalition of scientists, organizers, and storytellers working in 31 countries — coordinating the policy, communications, and frontline resources needed to keep 1.5°C within reach.

Our Mission

Three pillars. One deadline.

Climate Horizon Collective exists to compress the gap between climate science and political reality — by funding the people, evidence, and stories that move policy.

PILLAR 01

Rigorous science communication

We translate IPCC findings and peer-reviewed research into accessible briefings used by journalists, legislators, and 240,000 weekly subscribers to The Horizon Brief.

PILLAR 02

Frontline community support

We direct unrestricted funding, legal aid, and organizing capacity to communities on the receiving end of fossil-fuel infrastructure and climate disasters.

PILLAR 03

Structural policy change

We coordinate lobbying, litigation, and electoral programs targeting the federal, state, and corporate levers that determine whether emissions actually fall.

Scientific Advisory Board

The researchers who steer our work.

Our advisors review every major report and campaign brief. They are unpaid and independent, with no veto power over operations.

KM
Dr. Kate Marvel
Climate Modeler · Project Drawdown

Physicist specializing in cloud feedback and climate sensitivity. Author of "Human Nature: Nine Ways to Feel About Our Changing Planet."

SH
Dr. Saleemul Huq
Adaptation · ICCCAD, Bangladesh

Director of the International Centre for Climate Change and Development. Architect of the COP27 Loss & Damage Fund framework.

RB
Dr. Robert Bullard
Environmental Justice · TSU

Founder of the modern environmental justice movement. Distinguished Professor at Texas Southern University; advisor to the EPA on Justice40.

FO
Dr. Friederike Otto
Attribution Science · Imperial College

Co-lead of World Weather Attribution. Pioneered the rapid attribution methodology now used to link heatwaves and floods to fossil emissions.

JR
Dr. Johan Rockström
Earth Systems · PIK Potsdam

Director of the Potsdam Institute. Lead author on planetary boundaries framework and tipping-point cascades research.

AT
Dr. Ayana Elizabeth Johnson
Marine Biology · Urban Ocean Lab

Co-founder of Urban Ocean Lab, co-editor of "All We Can Save." Advisor on coastal resilience and blue-carbon policy.

The Science

The data is unambiguous.

What 13,000+ peer-reviewed studies and the IPCC AR6 report tell us about where we stand.

Visualization 03

Plain Language

Five key findings from IPCC AR6.

The Sixth Assessment Report is the most comprehensive scientific consensus ever assembled on Earth's climate. Here's what it actually says.

Finding 01

Human influence is unequivocal.

For the first time, the IPCC drops all hedging language. Greenhouse gas emissions from human activity have warmed the atmosphere, ocean, and land. There is no longer a credible alternative explanation.

Finding 02

The 1.5°C carbon budget is nearly spent.

At current emissions of ~40 GtCO₂/year, the remaining budget for a 50% chance of limiting warming to 1.5°C will be exhausted in approximately 5–7 years. Every ton matters.

Finding 03

Tipping points are closer than thought.

Five major tipping elements — Greenland ice sheet, West Antarctic ice sheet, Amazon rainforest, coral reefs, and boreal permafrost — could be triggered between 1.1°C and 1.5°C of warming.

Finding 04

Adaptation has hard limits.

Some impacts — saltwater intrusion, glacier loss, species extinction — cannot be adapted to. Adaptation buys time but is not a substitute for cutting emissions at the source.

Finding 05

Solutions exist and are cost-effective.

Solar and wind are now the cheapest sources of new electricity in 90% of the world. Cutting emissions in half by 2030 is technically and economically feasible — what's missing is political will.

Finding 06

Climate justice is not optional.

The countries least responsible for emissions face the worst impacts first. AR6 explicitly frames equitable adaptation finance as a precondition for effective global action.

Common Questions

Addressing misconceptions.

Click any question to expand. Each answer is reviewed by our Scientific Advisory Board.

Isn't the climate always changing? Why blame humans now?

Yes, Earth's climate has changed before — over thousands to millions of years, driven by orbital cycles, volcanic activity, and solar variation. What's different now is the rate and the cause. The current warming is occurring 10× faster than at any point in the last 65 million years, and the chemical fingerprint of the extra CO₂ in our atmosphere shows it came from burning fossil fuels.

What about volcanoes? Don't they emit more CO₂ than humans?
Won't technology — carbon capture, geoengineering — save us?
Is it already too late to do anything?
Aren't individual actions pointless against corporations?
If global temperature has only risen 1.2°C, why does it feel so much worse?
How can scientists predict 2100 when they can't predict next week's weather?
What about cosmic rays, the sun, or natural cycles?
References

Sources cited on this page.

[01]

Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis. Cambridge University Press, 2021.

[02]
NASA GISTEMP v4

Goddard Institute for Space Studies Surface Temperature Analysis, 2024 update.

[03]
NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory

Mauna Loa CO₂ record and global marine boundary layer data, accessed Oct 2024.

[04]
EM-DAT — CRED Disasters Database

Université catholique de Louvain. Decadal disaster event compilation, 1980–2024.

[05]
Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S)

2024 European State of the Climate Bulletin, ECMWF.

[06]
World Weather Attribution

Rapid attribution analyses on the 2024 North American heat dome event.

[07]
IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report

Summary for Policymakers, March 2023.

[08]
USGS Volcanic Hazards Program

Global volcanic CO₂ emission estimates, Gerlach et al.

content.text:
All five HTML pages built and saved to `/app/site/`:

- **home.html** — Hero with carbon-budget alert, countdown counter strip, stats row (CO₂/temp/bills), three campaign cards, impact dashboard, three stories of change, coral donate band with monthly tabs, newsletter signup, and footer.
- **about.html** — Hero with five intro stats, three-pillar mission cards, six-advisor scientific board with colored initial avatars, five-person exec team grid, donut chart financial breakdown, third-party ratings, "As reported in" media row, annual report band, and footer.
- **action.html** — Hero with time-commitment list, dark stats strip, featured petition with signature progress bar, call-your-rep with script preview, carbon footprint calculator with sliders + dark result card, US chapter map with events sidebar, role-picker form, three-card share toolkit, monthly donor band, and footer.
- **science.html** — Centered hero, attribution-science quote band, SVG line chart of global temp anomaly with Paris threshold line, two-bar disaster-count chart, sea-level rise visualization with timeline points, six IPCC findings cards, FAQ accordion (one open), dark references section, and footer.
- **stories.html** — Hero, world-map reporting locations with topics sidebar, cover-story split layout, dark italic pull-quote band, "Latest dispatches" grid with category tabs, video portraits row with play buttons, "The Horizon Dispatch" subscribe band, and footer.

Each file is self-contained with Google Fonts (Lora serif, Inter sans, JetBrains Mono) imported in `<style>`, and no external images — all visuals built from CSS gradients, shapes, and inline SVG.
